questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India is described as a:
questions.explanation: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. India is not a Presidential Republic (it has a parliamentary system). It is not a Constitutional Monarchy (it has an elected head of state). It is not a Federal Theocracy (it is secular).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Parliament of India:

(i) It consists of the President, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha.
(ii) The Lok Sabha is the lower house directly elected by the people.
(iii) The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body that is never fully dissolved.
(iv) The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 500 members.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha (Article 79). (ii) is correct — Lok Sabha members are directly elected by citizens. (iii) is correct — Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber; 1/3 of its members retire every 2 years but it is never fully dissolved. (iv) is wrong — the maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 552 (530 from states + 20 from UTs + 2 nominated Anglo-Indians, though the latter was discontinued).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The President of India is elected by:
options: Direct election by all citizens above 18 years
An electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.correctAnswer: An electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is indirectly elected by an electoral college comprising elected members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and all State Legislative Assemblies (Article 54). It is not a direct public election. It is not Rajya Sabha alone. The PM/Council don't elect the President.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India follows a parliamentary form of government.
Reason (R): In a parliamentary system, the executive (Council of Ministers) is collectively responsible to the legislature (Lok Sabha) and must maintain its confidence.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — India has a Westminster-style parliamentary system. (R) is correct — collective responsibility to the lower house is the defining feature. (R) explains (A) because collective responsibility to the legislature is precisely what distinguishes parliamentary systems from presidential ones.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following democratic institutions with their primary functions:

Column I:
(a) Lok Sabha
(b) Rajya Sabha
(c) Supreme Court
(d) Election Commission

Column II:
(i) Guardian of the Constitution and final court of appeal
(ii) Directly elected lower house — makes laws and controls finance
(iii) Conducts free and fair elections
(iv) Council of States representing federal interests

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha is the directly elected lower house controlling finance (ii). Rajya Sabha represents states (iv). Supreme Court is guardian of the Constitution (i). Election Commission conducts elections (iii). Option 2 swaps Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Option 3 swaps Rajya Sabha and Supreme Court. Option 4 swaps Lok Sabha and Election Commission.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Prime Minister of India is appointed by:
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1), the PM is appointed by the President (typically the leader of the majority party/coalition in Lok Sabha). The PM is not directly elected by people (they elect MPs). The CJI administers oaths but doesn't appoint the PM. The Speaker presides over Lok Sabha but doesn't appoint the PM.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are features of a federal system of government?

(i) Division of powers between central and state governments.
(ii) Written and rigid constitution.
(iii) Independent judiciary to interpret the constitution.
(iv) All powers concentrated in a single central authority.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — federalism requires division of powers between levels of government. (ii) is correct — a written constitution delineates powers clearly. (iii) is correct — an independent judiciary arbitrates disputes between Centre and States. (iv) is wrong — concentration of all power in a single authority is the characteristic of a UNITARY system, the opposite of federalism.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of how many members?
questions.explanation: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members (238 elected by state/UT legislatures + 12 nominated by the President for expertise in literature, science, art, social service). 238 is only the elected members. 245 is the current actual strength. 260 is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Judiciary in India:

(i) The Supreme Court is the apex court and final court of appeal.
(ii) High Courts exist at the state level, one for each state or group of states.
(iii) The judiciary is independent of the executive and legislature.
(iv) Judges of the Supreme Court are elected by popular vote.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Supreme Court is at the top of the judicial hierarchy. (ii) is correct — 25 High Courts serve states/UTs. (iii) is correct — judicial independence is a basic feature of the Constitution. (iv) is wrong — SC judges are appointed by the President on the recommendation of the collegium (CJI + senior judges), NOT elected by the public.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha does not vote ordinarily during proceedings.
Reason (R): The Speaker casts a vote only in case of a tie (casting vote) to maintain impartiality in conducting House proceedings.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Speaker refrains from voting in normal circumstances. (R) is correct — the casting vote in case of a tie ensures impartiality. (R) explains (A) because the reason the Speaker doesn't normally vote is precisely to maintain the impartiality needed to preside fairly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In a Presidential form of government, the President is:
options: A ceremonial head with no real power
Both the head of state and head of government with real executive power
Elected by the legislature and responsible to it
questions.correctAnswer: Both the head of state and head of government with real executive power
questions.explanation: In a presidential system (like the USA), the President combines the roles of head of state and head of government with real executive authority. 'Ceremonial head' describes a parliamentary president (like India's). 'Elected by legislature' describes a parliamentary PM. 'Appointed by judiciary' doesn't apply to any standard system.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following countries has a Presidential form of government?
questions.explanation: The USA has a presidential system where the President is directly elected and holds real executive power. The UK has a parliamentary system (PM responsible to Parliament). India has a parliamentary system. Japan has a parliamentary constitutional monarchy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

(i) It is an independent constitutional body established under Article 324.
(ii) It consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
(iii) It conducts elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of President and Vice-President.
(iv) The CEC can be removed by the President without any cause.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 324 establishes the Election Commission. (ii) is correct — it's a multi-member body (CEC + ECs). (iii) is correct — it superintends all these elections. (iv) is wrong — the CEC can only be removed through impeachment (same procedure as a Supreme Court judge), NOT by the President unilaterally.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following forms of government with their key features:

Column I:
(a) Democracy
(b) Monarchy
(c) Dictatorship
(d) Oligarchy

Column II:
(i) Rule by a single hereditary ruler
(ii) Rule by a small group of powerful people
(iii) Rule by the people through elected representatives
(iv) Absolute rule by one person who seized power, with no accountability

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Democracy is rule by the people through representatives (iii). Monarchy is rule by a hereditary ruler (i). Dictatorship is absolute rule by one person without accountability (iv). Oligarchy is rule by a small powerful group (ii). Option 2 swaps democracy and monarchy. Option 3 swaps monarchy and dictatorship. Option 4 swaps democracy and oligarchy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term of the Lok Sabha is:
questions.explanation: The normal term of Lok Sabha is 5 years from its first meeting (Article 83), unless dissolved earlier. It can be extended during a national emergency by one year at a time. 4 years is for some state assemblies in other countries. 6 years is the term for Rajya Sabha members. 'Permanent body' applies to the Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about local self-government (Panchayati Raj) in India:

(i) The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992, gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
(ii) It provides for a three-tier system: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zila Parishad.
(iii) Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the State Election Commission.
(iv) Panchayats have been given powers to levy and collect all central taxes.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the 73rd Amendment (Part IX) constitutionalized Panchayati Raj. (ii) is correct — three-tier system for states with population above 20 lakh. (iii) is correct — State Election Commissions (Article 243K) conduct panchayat elections. (iv) is wrong — Panchayats can levy local taxes as authorized by state legislatures, NOT central taxes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian President is the nominal/constitutional head, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head.
Reason (R): Under Article 74, the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the President is the formal head while the PM exercises real power. (R) is correct — Article 74 mandates the President to act on ministerial advice. (R) explains (A) because the constitutional requirement to follow the PM's advice is precisely what makes the President nominal and the PM the real executive.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which constitutional body advises the President on matters referred to it?
questions.explanation: Under Article 143, the President can seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on questions of law or fact. NITI Aayog advises on economic policy but is not a constitutional advisory body to the President on legal matters. Rajya Sabha is a legislative body. CAG audits accounts but doesn't advise the President on references.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are features of a democratic government?

(i) Universal adult suffrage — every adult citizen has the right to vote.
(ii) Rule of law — everyone is equal before the law.
(iii) Periodic free and fair elections.
(iv) Power concentrated in one person with no elections.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — universal adult franchise is fundamental to democracy. (ii) is correct — rule of law ensures equality and accountability. (iii) is correct — periodic elections allow people to choose/change their representatives. (iv) is wrong — concentration of power in one person without elections is a dictatorship, the antithesis of democracy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of:
questions.explanation: Under Article 64, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Lok Sabha is presided over by the Speaker. NITI Aayog is chaired by the PM. The NDC is also chaired by the PM.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the difference between parliamentary and presidential systems:

(i) In a parliamentary system, the executive is responsible to the legislature.
(ii) In a presidential system, the executive is independent of the legislature.
(iii) In a parliamentary system, the head of state and head of government are the same person.
(iv) In a presidential system, there is separation of powers among three branches.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the PM/Cabinet must retain legislative confidence. (ii) is correct — the President has a fixed term independent of legislative support. (iv) is correct — strict separation between executive, legislature, and judiciary in presidential systems. (iii) is wrong — in parliamentary systems, the head of state (President/Monarch) and head of government (PM) are DIFFERENT persons.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following countries with their form of government:

Column I:
(a) United Kingdom
(b) China
(c) Saudi Arabia
(d) Switzerland

Column II:
(i) Absolute Monarchy
(ii) Communist one-party state
(iii) Parliamentary Constitutional Monarchy
(iv) Federal Republic with direct democracy elements

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: UK is a Parliamentary Constitutional Monarchy (iii) — monarch is ceremonial, PM governs. China is a Communist one-party state (ii) — CPC rules. Saudi Arabia is an Absolute Monarchy (i) — the King holds supreme power. Switzerland is a Federal Republic with direct democracy elements (iv) — uses referendums frequently.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
Reason (R): The Lok Sabha, being directly elected by the people, has overriding authority on financial matters as representatives of taxpayers.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Article 109 mandates Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha. (R) is correct — as directly elected representatives of taxpayers, Lok Sabha has primary authority over public finance. (R) explains (A) because the democratic principle of 'no taxation without representation' gives the directly elected house financial supremacy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Chief Minister of a state is appointed by:
questions.explanation: Under Article 164, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor (typically the leader of the majority party in the state assembly). The President appoints the PM, not CMs. The legislature doesn't formally appoint — it's done by the Governor. The PM has no constitutional role in CM appointment.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India:

(i) The CAG audits all government expenditure (Centre and States).
(ii) The CAG is appointed by the President.
(iii) The CAG reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament.
(iv) The CAG is a member of the Council of Ministers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — CAG audits all government receipts and expenditure (Article 149-151). (ii) is correct — appointed by the President under Article 148. (iii) is correct — CAG reports are submitted to Parliament and examined by PAC. (iv) is wrong — the CAG is an independent constitutional authority, NOT a member of the Council of Ministers. Independence from the executive is essential for impartial auditing.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Collective Responsibility' in a parliamentary democracy means:
options: Each minister is responsible only for their own department
All ministers are collectively responsible to the legislature — if one falls, all fall
Ministers are responsible to the judiciary
Only the Prime Minister is responsible to Parliament
questions.correctAnswer: All ministers are collectively responsible to the legislature — if one falls, all fall
questions.explanation: Collective responsibility (Article 75(3)) means the entire Council of Ministers stands or falls together — a vote of no-confidence against the government removes all ministers. Individual departmental responsibility is separate. Ministers are responsible to the legislature, not judiciary. It's not just the PM — the entire council is collectively responsible.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body in India?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog was created by a Cabinet resolution (executive order) in 2015, not by the Constitution. It is NOT a constitutional body. The Election Commission (Article 324), Finance Commission (Article 280), and UPSC (Article 315) are all established by the Constitution itself.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Governor of a state:

(i) The Governor is appointed by the President of India.
(ii) The Governor serves at the pleasure of the President.
(iii) The Governor is the constitutional head of the state.
(iv) The Governor must be an elected representative of that state.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 155: President appoints the Governor. (ii) is correct — Article 156: Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President. (iii) is correct — the Governor is the constitutional/ceremonial head of the state. (iv) is wrong — the Governor is NOT elected; they are appointed and need not even be from that state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following democratic bodies with the level at which they operate:

Column I:
(a) Gram Panchayat
(b) Municipal Corporation
(c) Lok Sabha
(d) Zila Parishad

Column II:
(i) National level
(ii) District level
(iii) Village level
(iv) Large city level

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Gram Panchayat operates at village level (iii). Municipal Corporation governs large cities (iv). Lok Sabha is the national legislature (i). Zila Parishad operates at district level (ii). Option 2 swaps village and city levels. Option 3 swaps city and national. Option 4 swaps village and district.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian judiciary has the power of judicial review.
Reason (R): Judicial review allows courts to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive actions, and declare them void if they violate the Constitution.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Indian courts exercise judicial review (Articles 13, 32, 226). (R) is correct — it accurately describes what judicial review entails. (R) explains (A) by defining the power and its purpose, which is precisely what the judiciary exercises.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The minimum voting age in India is:
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment Act, 1989, reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years. Every citizen who has completed 18 years can vote. 16 years is below the threshold. 21 was the previous age limit (before 1989). 25 is the minimum age to contest Lok Sabha elections, not to vote.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the concept of 'Separation of Powers':

(i) It divides government into three branches: Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary.
(ii) Each branch has distinct powers and functions.
(iii) It prevents concentration of power and provides checks and balances.
(iv) India follows a strict separation of powers with no overlap.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the three organs are Legislature, Executive, Judiciary. (ii) is correct — each has specific functions (lawmaking, implementation, adjudication). (iii) is correct — prevents tyranny through checks and balances. (iv) is wrong — India does NOT follow strict separation (unlike the USA); there are overlaps (e.g., ministers are also legislators, President has legislative functions).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A 'No Confidence Motion' against the government can be introduced in:
questions.explanation: A No Confidence Motion can only be moved in the Lok Sabha (the house to which the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible under Article 75). The Rajya Sabha cannot move such a motion. It's not in both houses. Courts don't deal with confidence motions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are essential elements of a democracy?

(i) Free press and freedom of expression.
(ii) Independent judiciary.
(iii) Multi-party system allowing political competition.
(iv) Hereditary succession of rulers.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — free press is vital for informed citizenry and accountability. (ii) is correct — independent judiciary protects rights and rule of law. (iii) is correct — political competition through multiple parties ensures choice. (iv) is wrong — hereditary succession is a feature of monarchy, not democracy; democracy requires elections.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Constitutional Amendments with their provisions:

Column I:
(a) 42nd Amendment (1976)
(b) 44th Amendment (1978)
(c) 73rd Amendment (1992)
(d) 61st Amendment (1989)

Column II:
(i) Reduced voting age from 21 to 18
(ii) Added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to Preamble; added Fundamental Duties
(iii) Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj
(iv) Removed Right to Property as Fundamental Right

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment added Socialist/Secular to Preamble and Fundamental Duties (ii). 44th Amendment removed Right to Property as FR (iv). 73rd Amendment constitutionalized Panchayati Raj (iii). 61st Amendment reduced voting age to 18 (i). Option 2 swaps 42nd and 44th. Option 3 swaps 44th and 73rd. Option 4 swaps 42nd and 61st.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Universal Adult Suffrage' means:
options: All adult citizens have the right to vote regardless of caste, religion, gender, or wealth
Only men above 25 years can vote
questions.correctAnswer: All adult citizens have the right to vote regardless of caste, religion, gender, or wealth
questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage grants every adult citizen (18+ in India) the right to vote without discrimination based on caste, religion, sex, education, property, or income. 'Only educated' is restricted suffrage. 'Only taxpayers' is property-based suffrage. 'Only men above 25' is both gender-discriminatory and age-restricted.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has an independent Election Commission to ensure free and fair elections.
Reason (R): If elections were conducted by the ruling party, there would be a conflict of interest and potential for rigging.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Election Commission is constitutionally independent. (R) is correct — party-conducted elections would invite manipulation. (R) explains (A) because the need to prevent conflict of interest and ensure fairness is precisely why an independent body was created.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992):

(i) It gave constitutional status to urban local bodies (Municipalities).
(ii) It provides for three types: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.
(iii) It mandates reservation of seats for SC/ST and women in urban local bodies.
(iv) It applies only to rural areas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the 74th Amendment (Part IXA) constitutionalized Municipalities. (ii) is correct — three tiers based on population: Nagar Panchayat (transitional), Municipal Council (smaller towns), Municipal Corporation (larger cities). (iii) is correct — reservations for SC/ST and not less than 1/3 seats for women. (iv) is wrong — the 74th Amendment applies to URBAN areas; the 73rd Amendment covers rural areas.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Anti-Defection Law' (10th Schedule) was added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, added the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) to curb political defections. The 42nd Amendment dealt with emergency-era changes. The 44th reversed some 42nd provisions. The 61st reduced voting age.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes 'Bicameralism'?
options: A legislature with only one house
A legislature with two houses (upper and lower)
A system where the judiciary has two levels
A government with two prime ministers
questions.correctAnswer: A legislature with two houses (upper and lower)
questions.explanation: Bicameralism means a two-chambered legislature (e.g., India's Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha, UK's Commons + Lords). A single-house legislature is 'unicameral'. Two judicial levels is just a hierarchy. Two PMs doesn't exist as a system concept.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:

(i) The AG is appointed by the President on the advice of the government.
(ii) The AG is the highest law officer of the government.
(iii) The AG can participate in Parliament proceedings but cannot vote.
(iv) The AG must be a member of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 76: appointed by the President. (ii) is correct — the AG is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India. (iii) is correct — the AG can attend and speak in either House but has no right to vote (Article 88). (iv) is wrong — the AG does NOT need to be an MP; they must be qualified to be appointed as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: In India, the executive power of the Union is vested in the __________ and is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
questions.explanation: Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President. However, under Article 74, the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM. The PM exercises real power but formally it's vested in the President. The CJI heads judiciary. The Speaker heads Lok Sabha proceedings.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following officers with who appoints them:

Column I:
(a) President of India
(b) Chief Justice of India
(c) Governor of a State
(d) Chief Election Commissioner

Column II:
(i) President (on collegium recommendation)
(ii) President (on PM's advice)
(iii) Electoral College
(iv) President

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: President is elected by the Electoral College (iii). CJI is appointed by the President on collegium recommendation (i). Governor is appointed by the President on PM's advice (ii). CEC is appointed by the President (iv). Option 2 swaps President's election and CJI's appointment. Option 3 swaps CJI and Governor. Option 4 swaps President and Governor.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the types of majority in Parliament:

(i) Simple majority — more than 50% of members present and voting.
(ii) Absolute majority — more than 50% of the total strength of the house.
(iii) Special majority — 2/3rd of members present and voting (used for constitutional amendments).
(iv) All bills require a special majority for passage.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — simple majority is needed for ordinary bills. (ii) is correct — absolute majority is majority of total house strength. (iii) is correct — constitutional amendment bills (Article 368) require special majority. (iv) is wrong — ordinary bills only need simple majority; only constitutional amendments need special majority.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.
Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body where members serve staggered 6-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — unlike Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha is never dissolved. (R) is correct — staggered terms ensure continuity (1/3 retire biennially, maintaining 2/3 experienced members). (R) explains (A) because the staggered rotation system is what makes dissolution unnecessary and impossible — the house continuously renews itself.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the highest civil court in a district?
questions.explanation: The District Court (presided by the District Judge) is the highest civil court at the district level. The Supreme Court is at the national level. The High Court is at the state level. Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution forum, not a regular court in the hierarchy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the difference between a republic and a monarchy:

(i) In a republic, the head of state is elected (directly or indirectly).
(ii) In a monarchy, the head of state inherits the position.
(iii) A republic guarantees that no position is held by hereditary right.
(iv) All monarchies are absolute — the monarch has unlimited power.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — republic = elected head of state (like India, USA). (ii) is correct — monarchy = hereditary succession (like UK, Japan). (iii) is correct — 'republic' means no hereditary political authority. (iv) is wrong — NOT all monarchies are absolute; many are constitutional monarchies where the monarch's power is limited by a constitution and parliament (UK, Japan, Sweden).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments are often called the 'power to the __________' amendments.
questions.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Amendments empowered grassroots-level democratic institutions (Panchayats and Municipalities), bringing governance closer to the people. They don't empower the judiciary (that's through judicial review). They don't empower the executive (PM/Cabinet). They have nothing to do with military power.

The following data shows voter turnout in Indian general elections:

| Election Year | Turnout (%) |
|---------------|-------------|
| 2004 | 58.1 |
| 2009 | 58.2 |
| 2014 | 66.4 |
| 2019 | 67.4 |

What is the approximate increase in voter turnout percentage from 2009 to 2019?
questions.explanation: Increase = 67.4 − 58.2 = 9.2 percentage points. Option 7.2 subtracts from 2014 (66.4−58.2=8.2, close but not exact match). Option 11.2 overcalculates. Option 13.2 greatly overcalculates.
